why_in_two_sentences: Our page answers the definitional query with a tighter mechanism (deactivation as a learned, pre-verbal suppression of the signal), a distinctive self-recognition entry point, and far deeper question coverage across 34 FAQs plus differential-diagnosis tables that neither competitor attempts. The second organic result was the UC Davis academic PDF, which is a scholarly book chapter rather than a competing general-audience landing page, so it was skipped and the next organic article, Attachment Project, was used in its place.
what_the_winner_does_that_we_dont: WebMD opens with a dated medical-reviewer byline (name, credential, review date) placed above the definition; add a visible author/credential line and last-updated date near the top of our page so the reader sees provenance before scrolling.

WebMD gives a scannable prevalence figure early (about 20% of adults report an avoidant style) sourced to a survey; our page deliberately withholds numbers, so consider one cited, well-caveated prevalence sentence in the 'How common' FAQ to match the stat that pulls this query.

Attachment Project lists the exact sub-questions the article will answer as a bulleted preview directly under the intro; add a short scannable 'what this page covers' contents list near the fold so scanners see coverage breadth immediately.

Both competitors carry a compact, explicitly labeled adult-symptoms checklist as a standalone scannable block; add a single consolidated bulleted signs/symptoms list as its own section rather than distributing signs across prose and tables.
Attachment Project cites named academic sources (Ainsworth, Bowlby, Mikulincer & Shaver) in a Sources block; add a short references/further-reading block to signal research grounding.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Explains the actual mechanism (deactivation suppresses the output while the attachment system stays intact, and runs pre-verbally) instead of just listing traits.
Provides differential-diagnosis tables separating avoidance from introversion, genuine independence, boundaries, and disinterest by timing.
Covers 34 specific searcher questions as FAQs, including long-tail phrasings (ghosting, texting vs calling, relief after a breakup, saying goodbye to an avoidant) neither competitor touches.
Distinguishes attachment pattern from avoidant personality disorder and states plainly that no page or quiz can diagnose.
Includes a concrete when-to-see-a-professional section and a step-by-step 'what loosens it' practice sequence.
Explicitly separates dismissive from fearful avoidance rather than conflating them, and corrects the common conflation of avoidant with 'not caring.'

above_the_fold.ours: H1 'What is avoidant attachment?' then a boxed 'short answer' that defines it as a learned strategy for turning down the signal, followed by an 'identify-box' of first-person sentences the reader may recognise and a seminar link; it answers the query directly and earns the next scroll through self-recognition.
above_the_fold.theirs: WebMD shows a dated medically-reviewed byline then a one-paragraph plain definition and an immediate 'What Is Avoidant Attachment Style?' subhead; it earns the scroll through visible authority and a fast, quotable definition.
above_the_fold.gap: Add a visible author-plus-credential line and a last-updated date beside our fold answer, since both competitors lead with dated provenance and ours shows none above the fold.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: What are the signs of avoidant attachment in children?

trust_signals: WebMD leads with a dated medical reviewer and cites prevalence and genetic statistics while Attachment Project cites named academic sources, whereas ours relies on a named founder with first-person practitioner experience but shows no citations or dated review, making our authority more personal and less externally sourced.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add a compact, scannable adult signs-and-symptoms checklist as its own labeled section plus a near-fold contents preview of the questions the page answers, so this high-volume definitional query surfaces our coverage the way both competitors' scannable lists do.
